In multimodal inference scenarios, input size can vary by two orders of magnitude (single image 114KB vs. 100 images 11.1MB), and corresponding inference time jumps from 1 second to 70 seconds. This huge variance makes synchronous calls nearly impossible to run stably — a 70-second long-tail request will tightly hold the connection, while all subsequent requests queue up waiting. The addition of SQS decouples the "producer-consumer" relationship: the submission side only sends messages and doesn't care about consumption speed; the consumption side pulls from the queue at its own pace, controlling concurrency via ESM MaximumConcurrency. This means that no matter how bursty the upstream traffic is, Bedrock always sees a smooth, controlled request stream.
